speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what are the guidelines for the media when approaching those affected by a major traumatic event to avoid interference in their recovery; (b) what special considerations are put in place in relation to minors; and (c) whether there are plans to revise these guidelines.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: When a traumatic incident occurs, students and staff are naturally very affected, and safeguarding their well-being must be the priority.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: At the same time, we understand the high level of public interest and concern, and appreciate that the media have the important responsibility of accurate news reporting, which can help prevent public panic, rumours or fake news from spreading.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: I echo Minister Chan’s sentiments during his Ministerial Statement on 27 July that the media has shown sensitivity and restraint in reporting the River Valley High School incident.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Doing so would have created additional stress for them at an already difficult time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The media was also encouraged to give the school the space to recover from the incident.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This includes not publishing any information that may inadvertently lead to the identification of any persons under the age of 18 who may be involved in subsequent Court proceedings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: We will continue to engage and work closely with the media to enable them to do their job even amidst such tragedies, while prioritising the well-being of those involved.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Should the public, victims or their families have concerns about media behaviour when a traumatic event occurs, what recourse do they have and what measures are being taken to educate them on the sort of recourse that they have?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We understand, of course, that this is after the fact and students and parents would rather not be put through this situation in the first place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we, therefore, appeal to the media and all members of the public to exercise empathy and good judgement in the situation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One point of clarification for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In relation to the most recent incident at River Valley High School, there was online feedback from students who felt harassed on the actual day of the incident as the media gathered outside.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Although the members of the media were doing their job, was there something more that MCI could have done to prevent this feeling of harassment on the part of the students and their contact with the media?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are fully aware of the anguish felt by the students and parents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I understand this was something that was causing pain to the staff and students, but we hope this is something we can continue to manage.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We must understand that it was not just the media, both mainstream as well as online media, but also members of the public, who gathered outside the school once the news broke to offer their condolences, support and expressions of sympathy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We continue to appeal to both media and well-intentioned members of the public to give the much needed space to affected students and staff in such situations.
